summary.text: Nancy De Boer is a Republican state representative from Holland, Michigan, who has represented District 86 since 2023 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
A former teacher, radio host and mayor of Holland, she chairs the House Education Committee in the 2025-2026 term.

paragraphs.text: De Boer was born in Grand Rapids and lives in Holland, and she earned a B.A. in secondary education from Calvin College.
Her career experience includes working as a middle and high school English teacher, a morning radio show co-host on WPNW The Pledge, and a host on WLNS-TV.
She co-founded the West Michigan Character Council and has served as assistant director of She Leads Michigan, on the Holland City Council, and as a trustee on the Michigan Municipal League Board.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she was elected Holland's mayor in 2015, the first woman to hold that position in the city's history.
De Boer took office in the Michigan House in 2023, succeeding Thomas Albert, and she won re-election in 2024 over Democrat Abby Klomparens with 56.1 percent of the vote.

In 2025 and 2026 she was assigned to the Education Committee, which she chairs, and to the Energy, Health Policy, and Rules and Competitiveness committees; in 2023 and 2024 she served on the Appropriations Committee.

In the survey, she listed conservative fiscal principles, public safety, protecting the Great Lakes and natural resources, bringing additional business to the area, and housing among her policy interests.
